title: Sample-size precision was constant in three bird drought abundance samples from a 2024 release
abstract: We checked whether less precise estimates show larger bird abundance declines under drought within six study samples. The 2024 public release supplies 179 records. Only 106 records in four samples have group sizes. Three samples have one size pair; Hawaii has two. Within all five size groups, a term based on the squared effect estimate accounts for all reported variance changes to rounding error. Pearson effect and standard-error correlations range from -0.987 to +0.469. Rank correlations have opposite signs in two samples. Thus within-group reported precision does not give a separate sample-size contrast. This follow-up uses records and variance formulas from a prior campaign audit. It adds correlations and a precision-support check. It does not establish or remove publication bias. Shared droughts, missing sizes, detection and unbalanced periods limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, hashes and external retrieval instructions are included. No pollution effect was tested.

display.caption: Effect and standard-error correlations differ between measures in two samples. Group sizes are missing for 73 of 179 records. These fixed-release summaries have no sampling intervals.
